doc.countdown_a11y_desc: The component renders a native `<time>` element with role="timer" whose dateTime attribute exposes the target moment as an ISO 8601 timestamp. An aria-label announces the remaining time in long natural units ("2 days 4 hours remaining") via the countdown.remaining translation key. Because role="timer" is implicitly aria-live="off", screen readers are not interrupted every second; users query the timer on demand.
doc.countdown_best_practice_1: Drive state changes from onComplete (enable a button, swap a banner) instead of running a parallel timer in the consumer; the component already ticks on exact second boundaries.
doc.countdown_best_practice_2: When fairness matters (sales, auctions), compute the target from a server-provided timestamp; a client-derived target inherits the user's clock skew.
doc.countdown_best_practice_3: Use baseDate for snapshots, screenshots, and tests to make the output deterministic, and paused when the surrounding UI is suspended (e.g. a hidden wizard step).
doc.countdown_choice_matrix_desc: Choose based on the direction and nature of the time being communicated:
doc.countdown_choice_progress_when: When expressing completion of a bounded task as a fraction (upload, wizard steps) rather than wall-clock time.
doc.countdown_choice_relativetime_when: When describing how long ago (or in how long) a single event happens in prose form ("3 minutes ago", "in 2 hours"), without per-second urgency.
doc.countdown_choice_self_when: When counting down to a known future moment matters: sale and auction deadlines, OTP resend waits, maintenance windows, event starts.
doc.countdown_completed_desc: When the target passes, completedContent replaces the digits and onComplete fires once. Without completedContent the timer simply stays at zero.
doc.countdown_content_guideline_1: Always pair the timer with a label that says what happens at zero ("Sale ends in", "Resend available in"). Bare digits force users to guess the consequence.
doc.countdown_content_guideline_2: Provide completedContent that states the outcome ("Sale ended", "You can now resend the code") instead of leaving a frozen 00:00 on screen.
doc.countdown_design_intent: Deadlines create urgency only when they are visibly moving: a static "ends July 14" is easy to ignore, while a ticking timer communicates both scarcity and exactly how much room is left to act. The component owns the whole timer lifecycle (ticking, pausing, completion callback) so consumers only declare the target moment, and tabular figures keep the layout stable while digits change every second.
doc.countdown_i18n_desc: Unit labels are generated by `Intl.NumberFormat` with style "unit" and follow the current i18next language (en / ja / pt) with no bundled locale data; any BCP 47 locale supported by the browser can be forced per instance via the locale prop. The screen-reader phrase uses the countdown.remaining translation key, which ships in en / ja / pt.
doc.countdown_keyboard_desc: Countdown is non-interactive static content and receives no keyboard focus. When wrapped in a link or button via asChild, the wrapping element's standard keyboard behavior applies.
doc.countdown_locale_desc: Unit labels come from Intl.NumberFormat and follow the current i18next language; the locale prop overrides it for a single instance.
doc.countdown_long_desc: Countdown renders the time left until a target moment and updates once per second, with each re-render aligned to the second boundary so no tick is skipped. The digital variant shows a compact colon-separated clock (04:12:33) that drops leading zero segments, while the units variant shows one labeled segment per unit for sale banners and maintenance notices. Unit labels are localized through the browser-native `Intl.NumberFormat` API, so no locale data needs to be bundled.
doc.countdown_motion_desc: No animation is applied; the digits swap once per second, with each re-render scheduled on the second boundary to avoid drift and skipped seconds. `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` prevents horizontal jitter as digits change. When the days or hours segment reaches zero it is dropped, so let the surrounding layout shrink naturally.
doc.countdown_otp_desc: The digital variant drops leading zero segments (00:45 rather than 00:00:45) and renders inline, so it fits inside button labels and helper text.
doc.countdown_paused_desc: paused suspends ticking without shifting the target moment; when unpaused, the timer snaps to the real remaining time.
doc.countdown_prop_asChild: If true, the component will be rendered as its child, merging its props onto that child.
doc.countdown_prop_baseDate: Reference point used as "now". When set, the countdown is frozen at that instant (useful for snapshots and tests).
doc.countdown_prop_completedContent: Content shown instead of the zeroed digits once the countdown ends.
doc.countdown_prop_fallback: Content shown when the target cannot be parsed.
doc.countdown_prop_locale: BCP 47 locale override for unit labels (e.g. "en", "ja", "pt-BR"). Defaults to the current i18next language.
doc.countdown_prop_onComplete: Called once when the remaining time reaches zero (also on mount if the target is already in the past). Not called when baseDate is set.
doc.countdown_prop_paused: Pauses the countdown while true. It resumes from the real remaining time (the target moment does not shift).
doc.countdown_prop_size: Size of the numbers and labels.
doc.countdown_prop_target: The moment the countdown ends, as a Date object, ISO 8601 string, or epoch milliseconds.
doc.countdown_prop_unitDisplay: Length of the unit labels in the "units" variant.
doc.countdown_prop_variant: "digital" renders a compact colon-separated clock (04:12:33); "units" renders one labeled segment per unit (days / hours / min / sec).
doc.countdown_responsive_desc: The component renders as an inline-flex group and adapts to its container. The widest state is the units variant with all four segments; reserve space for it or use the digital variant in cramped layouts. Digits use tabular figures, so the width stays stable within a given segment structure.
doc.countdown_scenario_1: Use the units variant in lg with the sale end as target and completedContent="Sale ended", so the banner resolves itself the moment the deadline passes.
doc.countdown_scenario_2: Combine with OtpInput: render a small digital timer inside the resend button label ("Resend in 00:45") and re-enable the button from onComplete.
doc.countdown_scenario_3: Count down to the start of a maintenance window in a Banner; onComplete can switch the page into the maintenance state without polling.
doc.countdown_sizes_desc: size controls the digit and label scale: sm for inline use next to text, md for cards, lg for hero and banner placements.
doc.countdown_static_desc: Providing baseDate freezes the reference "now" and disables ticking, which makes the output deterministic.
doc.countdown_title: Display the remaining time until a target moment as a live ticking timer, either as compact digits or as labeled unit segments.
doc.countdown_units_desc: variant="units" renders one labeled segment per unit. The days segment appears only while at least one day remains, and labels follow the unitDisplay prop (long / short / narrow).

doc.leaderboard_a11y_spec: The root is an <ol> (ordered list), so screen readers announce item count and position automatically. The rank badge is aria-hidden since the list position already conveys rank. A highlighted entry receives aria-current='true' to indicate the current user's position.
doc.leaderboard_best_practice_1: Limit the list to 10–20 entries. A very long leaderboard loses motivational impact; use pagination or a 'Your Rank' summary for larger datasets.
doc.leaderboard_best_practice_2: Always provide a unit label when the score's meaning is not obvious from context alone.
doc.leaderboard_choice_datagrid_when: When the data has multiple sortable columns, requires filtering, or ranking is one of several equally important dimensions.
doc.leaderboard_choice_list_when: When items have equal visual weight and ranking or scoring is not the primary concern.
doc.leaderboard_choice_matrix_desc: Choose based on how ranked data needs to be presented:
doc.leaderboard_choice_use_when: When displaying a ranked list where scores and position are the primary focus, especially with medal emphasis for top performers.
doc.leaderboard_content_guideline_1: Keep entry names concise. Long names are truncated with an ellipsis to preserve layout integrity.
doc.leaderboard_content_guideline_2: Choose a unit label that is immediately understood in context ('pts', 'km', 'sales'). Avoid technical abbreviations that users may not recognize.
doc.leaderboard_desc: Display a ranked list of entries with scores and medal highlights for the top three positions.
doc.leaderboard_design_intent: Rankings are a powerful motivational tool. Automatic medal styling for the top three creates instant visual hierarchy without extra consumer configuration. The highlight prop addresses a common UX need: helping users locate their own position within a long list.
doc.leaderboard_i18n_desc: All displayed text comes from consumer-provided props (name, score, unit). No internal strings are used. Pass translated values directly through props.
doc.leaderboard_keyboard_desc: Standard list keyboard navigation applies. Tab moves focus through interactive elements; list items are not focusable unless the consumer adds interactivity.
doc.leaderboard_long_desc: Leaderboard renders an ordered list of entries, each showing a rank badge, optional avatar, name, and score. Ranks 1–3 receive medal colors (gold, silver, bronze) automatically. A highlight flag marks the current user's row with the primary color scheme.
doc.leaderboard_motion_spec: No motion is applied by default. When entries are reordered after a score update, animate the list items using CSS transitions on the parent container.
doc.leaderboard_responsive_desc: The component fills its container width. Long names are truncated via text-overflow: ellipsis. Consider limiting the number of visible entries on narrow viewports.
doc.leaderboard_scenario_community: Community platform: Top contributors in a forum or learning app, reinforcing engagement through visible status.
doc.leaderboard_scenario_employee: Employee recognition: A monthly sales or performance board that motivates through visible ranking and medal highlights.
doc.leaderboard_scenario_game: Game or quiz: Display final rankings at session end so players can see their position relative to others.

doc.reaction_a11y_spec: Each reaction button uses aria-pressed to indicate active state. The container uses role='group' with an aria-label. Emoji meaning is conveyed via aria-label, not just the visual glyph.
doc.reaction_best_practice_1: Sort reactions by count descending to surface the most resonant ones first.
doc.reaction_best_practice_2: Show the add-reaction (+) button only when a full reaction picker is also available, to avoid a dead-end interaction.
doc.reaction_choice_alt_when: Use a Like button when a single positive reaction is sufficient. Use Rating for numeric scoring.
doc.reaction_choice_matrix_desc: Choose based on the type of feedback interaction required.
doc.reaction_choice_use_when: When users need quick, expressive feedback options on social content, comments, or messages.
doc.reaction_content_guideline_1: Limit to 5–8 emoji options to avoid choice overload.
doc.reaction_content_guideline_2: Pair each emoji with an accessible label describing its meaning.
doc.reaction_desc: Display emoji reaction buttons with toggleable state and counts
doc.reaction_design_intent: Give users a lightweight way to express emotion without writing a comment. Familiar emoji reactions lower the barrier to engagement and humanize the interface.
doc.reaction_i18n_desc: Runtime strings use the 'common' namespace: reaction.aria_label, reaction.react_with, reaction.add_reaction. Emoji labels are provided by the consumer via the 'label' field of each ReactionItem.
doc.reaction_keyboard_desc: Each reaction button is focusable via Tab. Space or Enter toggles the reaction. The add-reaction button opens a picker when connected.
doc.reaction_long_desc: Reaction is an interactive component for expressing emotions or feedback through emoji buttons. Users can toggle individual reactions, and the count updates in real time.
doc.reaction_motion_spec: Scale up briefly on toggle to provide tactile feedback. Count updates without layout shift.
doc.reaction_responsive_desc: Reactions wrap automatically when space is constrained. Use 'sm' size on mobile to maintain touch targets.
doc.reaction_scenario_content: Documentation or article: Allow readers to react to sections, providing lightweight feedback to authors.
doc.reaction_scenario_message: Chat message: Show emoji reactions inline below a message bubble for quick feedback without typing.
doc.reaction_scenario_social: Social feed: Show reactions below a post. Users can see what others have added and toggle their own.
doc.relativeTime_a11y_desc: The component renders a native `<time>` element whose dateTime attribute exposes the exact ISO 8601 timestamp to assistive technologies and crawlers. The visible text is plain content read naturally by screen readers, and the native title tooltip provides the absolute date and time on hover for sighted users.
doc.relativeTime_best_practice_1: Keep the default live updates for long-lived views such as dashboards and feeds; pass live={false} or a fixed baseDate when rendering snapshots (server-side rendering, screenshots, tests).
doc.relativeTime_best_practice_2: Do not override the locale per instance without reason. Leaving locale unset lets the label follow the app-wide i18next language, keeping all timestamps consistent.
doc.relativeTime_best_practice_3: For legally or operationally significant events (payments, audit logs), show the absolute date next to the relative phrase instead of relying on the tooltip alone.
doc.relativeTime_choice_calendar_when: When users need to locate or pick dates within a monthly or weekly structure.
doc.relativeTime_choice_matrix_desc: Choose based on how the point in time needs to be communicated:
doc.relativeTime_choice_self_when: When the recency of a single event matters more than its exact date, such as posts, comments, notifications, or "last updated" labels.
doc.relativeTime_choice_timeline_when: When presenting an ordered sequence of events with descriptions, where the relationship between events is the focus.
doc.relativeTime_content_guideline_1: Place the component right after the content it qualifies (author name, action label). The phrase itself is generated by the browser and must not be concatenated with hand-written fragments of the same sentence.
doc.relativeTime_content_guideline_2: Prefer numeric="auto" (the default) for a natural tone ("yesterday") in feeds, and numeric="always" ("1 day ago") in dense data tables where uniform wording aids scanning.
doc.relativeTime_design_intent: Timestamps in feeds, chats, and tables are scanned, not read: "3 minutes ago" answers "how fresh is this?" faster than an absolute date. Delegating the wording to `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` guarantees grammatically correct phrases in every supported language (en / ja / pt and beyond) with zero bundled locale data, while the title tooltip and dateTime attribute keep the exact moment available to users and machines.
doc.relativeTime_format_desc: format="short" (or "narrow") abbreviates the unit, which suits dense tables.
doc.relativeTime_future_desc: Dates in the future are phrased accordingly ("in 2 hours").
doc.relativeTime_i18n_desc: Formatting is fully delegated to `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` and `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, which follow the current i18next language (en / ja / pt) automatically and require no translation keys. Any BCP 47 locale supported by the browser can be forced per instance via the locale prop.
doc.relativeTime_keyboard_desc: RelativeTime is non-interactive static text and receives no keyboard focus. When wrapped in a link or button via asChild, the wrapping element's standard keyboard behavior applies.
doc.relativeTime_locale_desc: The locale prop overrides the i18next language for a single instance.
doc.relativeTime_long_desc: RelativeTime converts a date into a human-friendly relative phrase using the browser-native `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` API, so no locale data needs to be bundled. It renders a semantic `<time>` element with a machine-readable dateTime attribute, shows the absolute date and time in a native tooltip, and re-renders itself as time passes so the label never goes stale.
doc.relativeTime_motion_desc: No animation is applied. Live updates simply swap the text at an interval matched to the displayed granularity (every second under a minute, every 15 seconds under an hour, every minute under a day, then hourly). `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` prevents horizontal jitter when digits change.
doc.relativeTime_numeric_desc: numeric="always" forces numeric phrases such as "1 day ago" instead of "yesterday".
doc.relativeTime_responsive_desc: The component renders a single inline text node and adapts to any container. In cramped layouts, use format="short" or "narrow" to reduce width instead of truncating.
doc.relativeTime_scenario_1: Activity feed or chat: show "5 minutes ago" next to each message so users can judge freshness at a glance; the label ticks forward automatically while the view stays open.
doc.relativeTime_scenario_2: Admin table: render a "Last updated" column with numeric="always" and format="short" for compact, uniform labels, while the tooltip reveals the precise timestamp for auditing.
doc.relativeTime_sentence_desc: The component renders an inline `<time>` element, so it can be embedded in surrounding text.
doc.relativeTime_static_desc: Providing baseDate freezes the reference point and disables live updates, which makes the output deterministic.
doc.relativeTime_title: Display a timestamp as a localized relative phrase such as "3 minutes ago" or "yesterday", kept up to date automatically.
doc.relativeTime_units_desc: The largest fitting unit is chosen automatically, from seconds up to years.

doc.visuallyhidden_a11y_desc: You can use Chrome DevTools to verify how content in the `VisuallyHidden` component is recognized by screen readers.
doc.visuallyhidden_a11y_step_1_desc: Right-click on the part where `VisuallyHidden` is used in the browser and select "Inspect" to open DevTools.
